# Incremental maintenance {.dark-slide background-color="#111C26"}

[BLOCK 6 &middot; PART B]{.eyebrow}

::: {.accent-bar}
:::

[Adding, updating, and removing packages in a site library.]{.subhead}

## Set up a site library

::: {.demo-label}
Live
:::

Same container as the local repository block, so `/opt/pkgrepo` is still
there.

```bash
mkdir -p /opt/rlibs/4.6

cat >> /usr/lib/R/etc/Rprofile.site <<'EOF'
.Library.site <- "/opt/rlibs/4.6"
EOF
```

Two ways to set the site library
([R-admin](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html#Managing-libraries)):

| | `.Library.site` in `Rprofile.site` | `R_LIBS_SITE` in `Renviron.site` |
|---|---|---|
| R-admin | Recommended | "Not recommended" |
| After startup | Locked; users cannot easily change it | Overridable per job with `${R_LIBS_SITE-...}` |
| Under `--vanilla` | Not applied (`Rprofile.site` is skipped) | Applied only if set in the job's environment |

```bash
# the environment-variable route
R_LIBS_SITE=${R_LIBS_SITE-'/opt/rlibs/4.6'}
```

## Check `.libPaths()`

```bash
R -q --no-echo -e '.libPaths()'
```

```text
[1] "/opt/rlibs/4.6"
[2] "/usr/lib/R/library"
```

The Debian site libraries are gone from the path: `.Library.site` replaced
them.

## Install, then lock down

```r
install.packages(c("xml2", "R6"), lib = "/opt/rlibs/4.6",
                 repos = "file:///opt/pkgrepo")
```

```bash
# readable by all, writable by root only
chown -R root:root /opt/rlibs/4.6
chmod -R a+rX,go-w /opt/rlibs/4.6
```

::: {.note}
[What `rocker/r-base` does instead]{.note-label}
It runs `chown root:staff /usr/local/lib/R/site-library` and `chmod g+ws`
(group-writable, setgid), so members of group `staff` can install into the
site library
([Dockerfile](https://github.com/rocker-org/rocker/blob/master/r-base/latest/Dockerfile)).
:::

## `old.packages()` before `update.packages()`

Say the repository now carries `rlang` 1.1.6 and the library has 1.1.5:

```r
old.packages(lib.loc = "/opt/rlibs/4.6",
             repos   = "file:///opt/pkgrepo")
```

```text
      Package LibPath          Installed Built   ReposVer Repository
rlang "rlang" "/opt/rlibs/4.6" "1.1.5"   "4.6.1" "1.1.6"  "file:///opt/pkgrepo/src/contrib"
```

`old.packages()` only reports: what is installed, what the repository
offers, and where it would come from. It changes nothing
([`?update.packages`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/update.packages.html)).

## `update.packages()` arguments

```r
update.packages(lib.loc = "/opt/rlibs/4.6",
                repos   = "file:///opt/pkgrepo",
                ask     = FALSE,
                checkBuilt = TRUE)
```

| Argument | What it does |
|---|---|
| `lib.loc` | Libraries to update. The default, `NULL`, means all of `.libPaths()` |
| `ask` | `TRUE` by default: asks for each package. `FALSE` for scripts |
| `checkBuilt` | Also treats packages built under an earlier R minor version as old. `FALSE` by default |
| `oldPkgs` | Only consider these packages |
| `instlib` | Install the updates into this library instead |

Source: [`?update.packages`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/update.packages.html).

## What `update.packages()` misses

**Only what it can see.** It compares the libraries in `lib.loc` with what
the repositories offer. A package the repository no longer carries is not
reported.

**Packages built under an older R.** Without `checkBuilt = TRUE`, a package
built under R 4.5 counts as current when its version number is current.

```r
# a library carried over from R 4.5
update.packages(lib.loc = "/opt/rlibs/4.6", checkBuilt = TRUE, ask = FALSE)
```

::: {.note}
[Managed site libraries]{.note-label}
Instead of updating in place, build a new repository and a new library,
check them as a cohort, and switch the symlink.
:::

## `remove.packages()` does not check dependents

```r
remove.packages("xml2", lib = "/opt/rlibs/4.6")
```

It removes the package and updates the index. It does not check whether
other packages depend on it
([`?remove.packages`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/remove.packages.html)).

```r
# check first
tools::package_dependencies("xml2", reverse = TRUE, which = "most",
  db = installed.packages(lib.loc = "/opt/rlibs/4.6"))
```

::: {.note}
[Check reverse dependencies first]{.note-label}
Packages that depend on a removed package stay installed, and fail when
loaded.
:::

## Verify a library

```r
# every installed package, and whether its dependencies resolve
ip <- installed.packages(lib.loc = "/opt/rlibs/4.6")
deps <- tools::package_dependencies(rownames(ip), db = ip)
missing <- setdiff(unlist(deps), c(rownames(ip),
                                   rownames(installed.packages(lib.loc = .Library))))
missing
```

```r
# can everything load?
for (p in rownames(ip))
  tryCatch(loadNamespace(p),
           error = function(e) cat("FAIL", p, conditionMessage(e), "\n"))
```

The first check reads metadata. The second loads each package, so it also
catches missing shared libraries.

## Environment variable reference

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `R_HOME` | The installation root. Set by R |
| `R_LIBS` | Library paths, used for the initial `.libPaths()` |
| `R_LIBS_USER` | The user library. Only used if the directory exists |
| `R_LIBS_SITE` | The site library. Prefer `.Library.site` in `Rprofile.site` |
| `R_ENVIRON`, `R_ENVIRON_USER` | Which environment files are read |
| `R_PROFILE`, `R_PROFILE_USER` | Which profile files are read |
| `R_DEFAULT_PACKAGES` | Packages attached at startup |
| `R_SCRIPT_DEFAULT_PACKAGES` | The same for `Rscript`; takes precedence |
| `TMPDIR` | The session's temporary directory, and where `configure` scripts run |

Sources: [`?EnvVar`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/EnvVar.html),
[`?.libPaths`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/libPaths.html),
[`?Rscript`](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/Rscript.html).

## A `noexec` `/tmp` breaks `configure`

::: {.note}
[From the R-admin manual]{.note-label}
"`TMPDIR` will be used to execute configure scripts when installing
packages, so if `/tmp` has been mounted as `noexec`, `TMPDIR` needs to be
set to a directory from which execution is allowed."
([R-admin](https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-release/R-admin.html#Running-R))
:::

```bash
# in Renviron.site, on a host with a noexec /tmp
TMPDIR=/var/tmp/R
```

The directory must exist and be writable. The same section also advises
setting `TMPDIR` for long-running jobs on systems that clean `/tmp`
periodically, for example with `tmpwatch`.

## `pak`

`pak` has a dependency solver, a system dependency solver, and parallel
downloads and installs ([pak](https://pak.r-lib.org/)).

```r
pak::pkg_install("xml2")
pak::pkg_deps_tree("dplyr")
pak::pkg_status("xml2")
pak::lockfile_create(c("xml2", "R6"), lockfile = "pkg.lock")
pak::lockfile_install("pkg.lock")
```

`install.packages()` ships with R; `pak` has to be installed first.

::: {.note}
[Recommendation]{.note-label}
Whichever you use for the site library, run it from a committed script.
:::
